messages:
mila: opening thread for postmortem follow-ups — we need to update the runbook and playbook for the worker memory-leak incident. main goals: clear triage steps, exact commands to run, and a simple escalation path. postmortem: https://redwood.postmortem/INC-2026-042

jamie: +1. i'll draft the triage checklist. thinking simple: 1) check pod memory, 2) capture pprof/gcore, 3) restart with isolation. will add commands.

sanjay: tagging for ownership — i can own the runbook triage section. deadline Fri 2026-04-02. i’ll include the minimal command set and a one-line summary to paste into pager messages. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: On-call for 2026-03-30 -> sanjay (SRE).

mila: sanjay, please include the quick escalation flow: who to page at >3x baseline OOMs in 10m. currently that’s devops oncall -> infra-leads -> eng-sre. we should make it explicit.

jamie: proposed triage snippet to add under "worker/memory" section:
```
1) kubectl -n svc get pods -o wide | grep worker
2) kubectl -n svc top pod <pod> --containers
3) kubectl -n svc logs <pod> --since=1h | grep -i oom
4) on node: sudo pmap -x <pid> | sort -k3 -n | tail -n 20
5) capture heap: curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap.pprof
6) if heap growth > 100MB/min, restart: kubectl -n svc rollout restart deploy/worker
```

sara: add note to runbook that restart is a mitigation only; include pointer to long-term fix owner (repo-level leak investigation).

jamie: also adding a short PagerDuty message template for the first 5m:
```
[INCIDENT] worker memory growth detected - pod <pod> > 3x baseline. Triage steps started. Oncall: <oncall>. See runbook: /docs/runbooks/worker-memory.md
```

mila: for escalation path, suggest:
- Step 1: oncall triages and runs the commands above (0-10m)
- Step 2: if restart fails or repeated OOMs within 10m, page infra-leads (10-20m)
- Step 3: if rollback required or cluster-level degradation, page eng-sre and exec (20-40m)
Make sure contacts and PD rotations are linked in runbook.

sanjay: added the escalation bullets to the runbook draft. also adding explicit paging commands (pd-ops):
```
pd trigger --service "worker" --severity critical --detail "Repeated OOMs after restart" --escalation "infra-leads"
```

mila: recurring-pattern note: we saw similar memory growth in three incidents in last 8 weeks (INC-2026-012, INC-2026-021, INC-2026-042). propose adding a monitoring rule: increase of resident_memory over 5m window > 100MB. example promql:
```
increase(process_resident_memory_bytes{job="worker"}[5m]) > 1e8
```
If alert triggers twice in 30m, auto-create an incident and set severity to P2.

jamie: good — i'll add the promql and the alert runbook entry. also will add a playbook checklist for post-restart verification (trace sampling, latency check).

sara: owners and deliverables:
- sanjay: runbook triage section + escalation commands (due 2026-04-02)
- jamie: promql alert + post-restart verification checklist (due 2026-04-05)
- mila: update incident template + link to postmortem (due 2026-04-05)

sanjay: noted. i'll push a PR to docs repo and request review from jamie and mila. brief PR title: "runbook: worker memory triage + escalation"

mila: thanks. one more ask — add a short troubleshooting snippet for when pod logs are truncated (how to fetch archived logs from fluentd). jamie can you add that?

jamie: will do. plan: add a 2-line fluentd fetch command and a pointer to log-archiver runbook.

mila: perfect. i'll follow up next week in the oncall retro to check closures. marking this thread as the canonical action tracker for this postmortem. :white_check_mark:
